title: M5 stage17: finite factor exclusion identity
scope: Exact finite inclusion-exclusion algebra; identifying forbidden polynomial-divisibility events remains separate

spec.name: M5.FiniteExclusion.filtered_powerset
spec.statement: ∀ (S : Finset M5.BinaryPolynomial) (bad : M5.BinaryPolynomial → Bool), S.powerset.filter (fun H => ∀ p ∈ H, bad p = true) = (S.filter (fun p => bad p = true)).powerset
spec.guidance: Extensionality, Finset.mem_filter, mem_powerset and subset_iff. Both sides describe subsets contained in the bad factor set. Return only tactic lines without leading by; preserve exact target.

spec.name: M5.FiniteExclusion.alternating_subsets
spec.statement: ∀ S : Finset M5.BinaryPolynomial, (∑ H ∈ S.powerset, (-1 : ℤ)^H.card) = if S = ∅ then 1 else 0
spec.guidance: Use Finset.sum_powerset_neg_one_pow_card (actual library may place theorem in Nat namespace: inspect import). Empty set gives1 and nonempty gives0. Return only tactic lines without leading by; preserve exact target.

spec.name: M5.FiniteExclusion.exclusion_indicator
spec.statement: ∀ (S : Finset M5.BinaryPolynomial) (bad : M5.BinaryPolynomial → Bool), M5.FiniteExclusion.exclusionSum S bad = if ∀ p ∈ S, bad p = false then 1 else 0
spec.guidance: Turn multiplying indicator into if on the summand, then Finset.sum_filter. Use filtered_powerset and alternating_subsets. The bad-filter is empty iff every Bool value on S is false. No assumptions of factor irreducibility here; polynomial mapping is a separate layer. Return only tactic lines without leading by; preserve exact target.
